paragraph: Granville’s 1960 timing system prints a neutral 50 out of 100 composite this morning, completely free of any breadth divergence warnings despite a fragmented tape. Internal market mechanics show a clear push-and-pull, highlighted by strong relative strength in equal-weight participation with RSP outperforming SPY by +1.12% and transports surging +1.89%, yet heavily offset by aggressive risk-off behavior as the VIX spikes +7.32% to a fearful 28.29 alongside a front-loaded skew (+11.1 pts) and backwardated term structure. Macro conditions compound this defensive posture, featuring widening high-yield credit spreads at 3.72% and a bearish defensive rotation where XLP outpaces XLY by +0.65% while high-beta issues lag significantly. Ultimately, despite resilient breadth and transport leadership, the overwhelming surge in market fear and credit stress dictates a cautious stance for the upcoming session. Expect a choppy, defensive-leaning bias as traders navigate elevated short-term volatility.
